concept.name: Pre-trade checklist
concept.definition: A short list of conditions verified immediately before entering a trade - setup validity, thesis, risk size, stop location, catalysts, and emotional state - designed to filter impulsive trades and enforce the trading plan at the moment of execution.
concept.intuition: Pilots do not take off on memory and gut feel; the checklist is the ten seconds that stops a FOMO click from becoming a trade.
concept.mechanics: Each item is a binary gate (for example: Is this a defined playbook setup? Is the stop placed? Is risk within limits? Am I calm?); any failed item blocks or defers the trade. Its value is forcing deliberation at the point where arousal and urgency peak.
concept.failure_modes: Checklists degrade into box-ticking when items are vague or when marginal answers are rationalized under urgency. They also add latency, which matters for very short-horizon strategies unless the checklist is rehearsed to automaticity.
concept.misconceptions: A checklist is not bureaucracy for beginners only; it exists precisely because expert intuition is least reliable under time pressure and arousal. Passing the checklist does not make the trade good - it only enforces minimum standards.
concept.example: Before buying a breakout, a trader confirms: setup in playbook, volume above threshold, stop at the structure low risking 0.4R of the daily limit, no major news in the next hour - then enters.
